A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 19-page paper, with readable text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. v3 Appendix A.1–A.9 maps directly to v4 Appendices A–I; no material gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original backdoor-detection experiments using o1-mini BigCodeBench solutions and Llama monitors in Sections 4–6, plus original distribution-shift evaluations in Appendix A.7.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental outcomes in Sections 4–6 and Appendix G, including comparisons of monitoring policies and their performance under distribution shift.

M1.justification: The exhaustive monitor-invocation search, Neyman–Pearson auditing procedure, and NP, NPS, and SR policy classes are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and its explanation are retained; Appendix A.6 becomes Appendix F.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate backdoor detection on o1-mini BigCodeBench solutions and on backdoors from Wen et al. (2025). The distribution-shift evaluation in v3 Appendix A.7 is retained as v4 Appendix G.

E2.justification: Figures 2–3 retain the naive, NP, and NPS comparisons. The SR comparisons retain the same single-monitor NPS baselines using Llama 8B or 70B and the always-both-monitors BM baseline, including in the appendix.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains 1,140 aligned and 318 misaligned responses, the 218/100 misaligned train/test split, fixed aligned data, monitor-score preprocessing, cost ratios, and recall/cost evaluation. The appendix's 300-backdoor distribution-shift protocol is also unchanged.

E4.justification: The audit-cost sensitivity study in Figure 3b, monitor-score and decision-boundary analyses, example backdoor, and distribution-shift analyses in Figures 8–10 are retained. Appendix renumbering introduces no new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 500 random train/test splits and quantile-based 90% confidence intervals in Section 4.1. The per-seed bootstrap comparison and 10% significance statement are unchanged between v3 Appendix A.1 and v4 Appendix A.

E6.justification: The plotted results in Figures 1–10 and numerical findings in the text match. For example, Section 5.2 retains 71% monitor usage and 2.4% overall audit false-positive rate for NPS, versus 1% for deterministic policies at the stated $1.20 budget and 20:1 audit-to-monitor cost ratio.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, Equations 1–9, Neyman–Pearson argument, alternative budget formulations, and computational-complexity analysis are unchanged. v3 Appendices A.2 and A.9 become v4 Appendices B and I without mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: cost-constrained monitoring optimization, more than doubling recall relative to a naive baseline in the demonstrated setting, and Pareto benefits from combining monitors.

C2.justification: The explanations of nonmonotonic monitor scores and monitoring/auditing tradeoffs are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same distribution-mismatch, overfitting, and computational-scaling limitations and suggested mitigations; the distribution-shift interpretation is also retained.

D1.justification: The monitor prompts, 200-quantile search details, hardware specifications, runtimes, and code and practitioner-guide links are unchanged. Their appendix sections are renumbered and some text crosses different page breaks, without changing reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are unchanged. Both versions retain the same citations and positioning relative to AI control, costly classification, and likelihood-ratio-based classifier combination.

P1.justification: v4 promotes appendix subsections A.1–A.9 to sections A–I and updates cross-references. It revises author-contribution wording, expands acknowledgments with research-management and MARS support attribution, and replaces the preprint notice with NeurIPS 2025 conference information. The scientific narrative is unchanged.

P2.justification: Larger appendix headings and altered spacing shift figures and text vertically and change several page breaks, particularly in the hardware and complexity sections. Figure 1's appendix reference is updated, while all figure content, axes, legends, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 adds explicit MARS/Cambridge AI Safety Hub support attribution and revises credits and appendix presentation. These limited disclosure and editorial changes leave the scientific argument, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information intact, without a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
